title: Functoriality of the derived Mayer--Vietoris triangle
statement:
Let W be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme] with W=U\cup V, U and V quasi-compact open subschemes, and open immersions j_U, j_V, j_{UV}. For E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_W) [def-pc-derived-category] write MV(E) for the distinguished triangle E\to R(j_U)_*E|_U\oplus R(j_V)_*E|_V\to R(j_{UV})_*E|_{U\cap V}\xrightarrow{\delta_E}E[1] of [lem-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-triangle] [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Choose a K-injective complex \mathcal I^\bullet representing E whose terms are injective [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; by [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open] its restrictions are K-injective, and \delta_E is the boundary morphism that [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] attaches to the degreewise short exact sequence 0\to\mathcal I^\bullet\to j_{U,*}(\mathcal I^\bullet|_U)\oplus j_{V,*}(\mathcal I^\bullet|_V)\to j_{UV,*}(\mathcal I^\bullet|_{U\cap V})\to0, which is exact because the restriction maps of the injective modules \mathcal I^n are surjective [lem-sc-ringed-space-injective-restriction-surjective]. Then:
(1) (naturality in E) for every morphism \varphi:E\to F in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_W), the triple (\varphi,\ R(j_U)_*(\varphi|_U)\oplus R(j_V)_*(\varphi|_V),\ R(j_{UV})_*(\varphi|_{U\cap V})) is a morphism of distinguished triangles MV(E)\to MV(F); in particular \varphi[1]\circ\delta_E=\delta_F\circ R(j_{UV})_*(\varphi|_{U\cap V}).
(2) (compatibility with direct image) let h:W'\to W be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes, put U'=h^{-1}(U), V'=h^{-1}(V), assume W' quasi-compact and quasi-separated and U', V' quasi-compact, and let E'\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{W'}), so that Rh_*E'\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_W) [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh]. Then Rh_* applied to MV(E') for the cover W'=U'\cup V' is a distinguished triangle in D(\mathcal O_W), and the canonical isomorphisms Rh_*R(j_{T'})_*(E'|_{T'})\cong R(j_T)_*R(h|_{T'})_*(E'|_{T'})\cong R(j_T)_*((Rh_*E')|_T) for T\in\{U,V,U\cap V\}, T'=h^{-1}(T) [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition], together with the identity of Rh_*E', form an isomorphism of distinguished triangles Rh_*MV(E')\cong MV(Rh_*E'), compatible with the connecting morphisms Rh_*(\delta_{E'}) and \delta_{Rh_*E'}.

source.place: Tag 08BV construction from the degreewise short exact sequence of K-injective complexes; functoriality of the short-exact-sequence triangle

proof.text: Choose K-injective representatives \mathcal I^\bullet and \mathcal J^\bullet for E and F with injective terms [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. A morphism \varphi:E\to F is represented by a chain map u:\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J^\bullet because maps into a K-injective complex compute morphisms in the derived category [lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison]. The degreewise sequences defining MV(E) and MV(F) are short exact: left exactness is the sheaf axiom, and surjectivity on the right holds over every open because restriction maps of injective modules are surjective [lem-sc-ringed-space-injective-restriction-surjective]. By [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open] the restrictions of \mathcal I^\bullet and \mathcal J^\bullet to U, V and U\cap V are K-injective, so j_{T,*}(u|_T) represents R(j_T)_*(\varphi|_T) for T\in\{U,V,U\cap V\} [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Restricting u to U, V and U\cap V gives a morphism between the two short exact sequences. The naturality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] therefore gives a morphism of the two distinguished triangles, in particular \varphi[1]\circ\delta_E=\delta_F\circ R(j_{UV})_*(\varphi|_{U\cap V}).

source.place: Tag 08BV construction and functoriality of the short-exact-sequence triangle

proof.text: Choose a K-injective complex \mathcal I'^\bullet with injective terms representing E' and a K-injective complex \mathcal J^\bullet with injective terms representing Rh_*E', together with a quasi-isomorphism q:h_*\mathcal I'^\bullet\to\mathcal J^\bullet [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Apply the triangulated functor Rh_* to the distinguished triangle MV(E') [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. For T\in\{U,V,U\cap V\} restrict q to T and apply j_{T,*}. Since (h_*\mathcal I'^\bullet)|_T=h_{T',*}(\mathcal I'^\bullet|_{T'}) (elementary), the source is j_{T,*}h_{T',*}(\mathcal I'^\bullet|_{T'})=h_*j_{T',*}(\mathcal I'^\bullet|_{T'}), which represents Rh_*R(j_{T'})_*(E'|_{T'})\cong R(j_T)_*R(h_{T'})_*(E'|_{T'}) [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition] because \mathcal I'^\bullet|_{T'} is K-injective [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open]; the target j_{T,*}(\mathcal J^\bullet|_T) represents R(j_T)_*((Rh_*E')|_T), and q|_T realizes the isomorphism R(h_{T'})_*(E'|_{T'})\cong(Rh_*E')|_T of [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open]. Thus these components give the asserted isomorphisms on the second and third terms, while the first term is identified by the identity of Rh_*E'.

source.place: Tag 0DJ9 induction step, identification of relative Mayer--Vietoris terms after derived direct-image composition

proof.text: The sequence 0\to\mathcal I'^\bullet\to j_{U',*}(\mathcal I'^\bullet|_{U'})\oplus j_{V',*}(\mathcal I'^\bullet|_{V'})\to j_{U'V',*}(\mathcal I'^\bullet|_{U'\cap V'})\to0 defining MV(E') is split in every degree because each \mathcal I'^n is injective (elementary). Its terms are K-injective: \mathcal I'^\bullet|_{T'} by [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open], its image under j_{T',*} because j_{T',*} is right adjoint to the exact restriction functor [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], and a finite direct sum of K-injective complexes is K-injective (elementary). Hence [lem-pc-derived-functor-termwise-split-ses-triangle] applied to F=h_* identifies Rh_*MV(E'), including Rh_*(\delta_{E'}), with the triangle of the image sequence 0\to h_*\mathcal I'^\bullet\to\cdots\to0. The map q of Step 2 and its restrictions give a morphism of short exact sequences from this image sequence to the sequence defining MV(Rh_*E') with the representative \mathcal J^\bullet, whose components are the isomorphisms of Step 2. The naturality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] applied to this morphism gives Q(q)[1]\circ Rh_*(\delta_{E'})=\delta_{Rh_*E'}\circ(\text{the intersection-term isomorphism}). Thus the three component isomorphisms form an isomorphism of distinguished triangles Rh_*MV(E')\cong MV(Rh_*E'), compatible with the connecting morphisms.
